## Installing RIANA

RIANA needs Python 3.10 or newer. We recommend a virtual environment.

```bash
$ pip install riana
```

Two optional extras add the desktop app and the DIA-NN reader:

```bash
$ pip install "riana[gui]"   # PySide6 desktop app (riana gui)
$ pip install "riana[dia]"   # DIA-NN report.parquet intake
```

Check the installation and list the commands:

```bash
$ riana --help
```

From a clone of the repository, a single bovine serum albumin run (Q-Exactive) integrates in
seconds and writes `out/test/time0_riana.txt`:

```bash
$ riana integrate tests/data/sample1/ tests/data/sample1/percolator.target.psms.txt -q 0.1 -o out/test/
```


## Preparing the inputs

RIANA does not search spectra itself. Run the identification upstream: **quantms** for DDA (it
writes an mzTab) or **DIA-NN** for DIA (it writes a `report.parquet`). RIANA reads those
identifications and extracts the MS1 isotopomers from the mzML files itself.

:::{.callout-tip}
## Mass spectrometry files

RIANA reads mzML (plain or gzipped). Convert vendor files (e.g., Thermo `.raw`) with `msconvert`
from [ProteoWizard](https://proteowizard.sourceforge.io/), with peak picking on, so MS1 is
centroided: the integration mass window assumes centroid data and is taken from the SDRF's
precursor mass tolerance by default.
:::

### The SDRF sample sheet

An [SDRF](https://github.com/bigbio/proteomics-sample-metadata) sample sheet (`.sdrf.tsv`, one row
per run, or per channel for multiplexed runs) describes the experiment. quantms uses the same
sheet. RIANA reads these columns and ignores the rest:

| Column | Used for |
|---|---|
| `comment[data file]` | Joins the row to its mzML file (extension ignored). |
| `source name` | The sample. |
| `characteristics[labeling time]` | The labeling time, e.g. `7 day` (time-series experiments). |
| `characteristics[mixing proportion]` | Instead of labeling time, for labeled/unlabeled mixing calibrations. |
| `characteristics[biological replicate]` | Biological replicate number; replicates stay separate points in the fit. |
| `characteristics[individual]` | Optional: the animal a sample came from (see below). |
| `factor value[...]` | The condition (several factor columns are joined with `|`). |
| `characteristics[precursor enrichment]` | Precursor enrichment, e.g. `0.046` for 4.6 % body-water D~2~O. |
| `comment[proteomics data acquisition method]` | DDA or DIA. |
| `comment[precursor mass tolerance]` | Integration mass window, e.g. `10 ppm`. |
| `comment[fraction identifier]`, `comment[technical replicate]` | Fractions and technical replicates of one sample, combined before fitting. |
| `comment[modification parameters]` | Modifications searched. |
| `comment[label]` | Multiplexing channel (TMT, dimethyl). |

Exactly one of labeling time or mixing proportion must be present.

**Animals.** If one animal provides several samples (e.g. four heart chambers), give it the same
`characteristics[individual]` on all of its rows, with IDs unique across groups. RIANA uses it for
the random animal effect of the interaction test (below). Without it, RIANA identifies an animal by
condition × labeling time × biological replicate, which is right only if each replicate number names
the same animal in every tissue and each animal is sampled at one time. Serial sampling of the same
animal needs real IDs.


## Running a project

Point `integrate` at the folder of mzML files, the identification file and the SDRF. RIANA writes one
`<run>_riana.txt` per run plus a `riana_manifest.tsv` that indexes the project. `fit` and `rollup`
read the manifest, so runs are grouped by their SDRF identity rather than by file name, and write
their outputs next to it (`-o` elsewhere forks a copy of the project there instead).

```bash
# 1. Integrate every run (one mzML in memory per worker)
$ riana integrate /path/to/mzml report.mzTab --sdrf samplesheet.sdrf.tsv \
    --workers 4 --out ./out

# 2. Fit each peptidoform's turnover curve
$ riana fit --manifest ./out/riana_manifest.tsv \
    --coefficients deberneh_2025_rss --depth 3 --workers 4

# 3. Roll peptides up to proteins
$ riana rollup --manifest ./out/riana_manifest.tsv --workers 4
```

For DIA, pass the DIA-NN `report.parquet` as the identification file; the SDRF declares the
acquisition as DIA. For DDA, `integrate --mbr` recovers timepoints a peptide missed by chance
(match-between-runs). `--coefficients` picks the labeling-site table; `deberneh_2025_rss` is
recommended for D~2~O, and ^18^O water uses its own tables (`--label o18`, see the
[Documentation](about.qmd)). The precursor enrichment comes from the SDRF; `--ria` overrides it.

### Comparing two conditions

```bash
$ riana rollup --manifest ./out/riana_manifest.tsv \
    --model "linear simple" --reference-condition control
```

`linear simple` fits each protein's conditions together and reports, per protein, the turnover
difference `delta_k` = k(test) − k(reference) with a p-value and a Benjamini–Hochberg-adjusted
`delta_k_p_adj`. With more than two conditions, name the pair with `--test-condition`.

### Several tissues from the same animals

Split the runs into one experiment per tissue at integration, then compare conditions within each:

```bash
$ riana integrate /path/to/mzml report.parquet --sdrf samplesheet.sdrf.tsv \
    --experiment-column "characteristics[organism part]" --workers 4 --out ./out
$ riana fit --manifest ./out/riana_manifest.tsv --coefficients deberneh_2025_rss
$ riana rollup --manifest ./out/riana_manifest.tsv --model "linear simple" \
    --reference-condition control --interaction --plot
```

- Δk is computed and BH-adjusted within each tissue.
- `--plot` writes a PDF of φ-space curves per tissue.
- `--interaction` also fits each protein across the tissues, with a random effect for the animal,
  and tests whether the condition effect differs between them (`riana_rollup_interaction.txt`).
  It compares two conditions.

### The desktop app

`riana gui` opens the same steps as forms: **Integrate** (with an *Experiment from* choice for
splitting runs by an SDRF column), **Model** (fit) and **Protein** (rollup, with the *Interaction*
option for `linear simple`). Each tab can load a project's saved results without recomputing, and
shows chromatograms, fitted curves and φ-space plots for the selected row.

### Single-run (Percolator) path

Without `--sdrf`, the identification file is read as a Percolator `target.psms.txt` for one mzML,
and the sample name carries the timepoint:

```bash
$ riana integrate /path/to/mzml percolator.target.psms.txt --sample time1 -o ./out
$ riana fit ./out/time0_riana.txt ./out/time1_riana.txt ./out/time3_riana.txt \
    --coefficients deberneh_2025_rss --ria 0.06 --out ./out
```


## Output

Every output file starts with a provenance header (RIANA version, settings, input).

| File | Contents |
|---|---|
| `<run>_riana.txt` | One row per identification, one column per integrated isotopomer (`iso0`, `iso1`, …), plus mass-accuracy columns. |
| `riana_manifest.tsv` | The project index: each run's identity and every stage's outputs. |
| `riana_fit_peptides.txt` | Per peptidoform: `k_deg`, its confidence interval, R², and point counts. |
| `riana_fit_fractions.txt` | Per peptidoform and timepoint: the fraction of new protein (θ, column `fs`) with its prediction interval. |
| `riana_rollup_proteins.txt` | Per protein (and experiment, condition): `k_deg`, and `delta_k` / `delta_k_p_adj` under `linear simple`. |
| `riana_rollup_fractions.txt` | The collapsed per-replicate, per-timepoint θ each protein was fitted on. |
| `riana_rollup_interaction.txt` | With `--interaction`: per-tissue k and Δk from the joint fit, and the interaction tests. |

Half-life is `ln(2) / k_deg`. Every option is listed in the [CLI Reference](reference.qmd).
